captions.detailed: A bicycle dropper seatpost with a long, dark-anodized outer tube and a slightly narrower inner stanchion tube. The inner tube slides telescopically inside the outer tube to adjust saddle height. At the top of the inner tube, a grey metal saddle rail clamp assembly is mounted, featuring a pivot mechanism to adjust the tilt of the saddle.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a trail dropper seatpost. It must feature a long black outer tube, a sliding inner post, and a grey saddle rail clamp at the top with a revolute tilt adjustment.
captions.factory: Construct the outer tube using a Cylinder primitive with a dark material. Model the inner tube as a slightly narrower, coaxial Cylinder with a metallic material. Create the saddle clamp assembly by combining small Box and Cylinder primitives to form the clamp body and rail jaws, then define a prismatic joint for the post's height travel and a revolute joint for the saddle tilt angle.
